title: A new approval precondition blocks operator-approved merges of PRs with legacy SHA-named reports

consumerGuidance.architecture: MARC's trusted controller is Node.js CommonJS with no runtime dependencies. Legacy SHA-named report evidence without reportCreatedAt remains unchanged and verifiable; never rename history. Operator approval may be supplied to merge after the report pair is published.
consumerGuidance.notes: Reduced from PR16 to the two controller files that own approval publication; the other PR16 files do not affect this behavior.

mustCite: the new `if (!e.reportCreatedAt) throw` guard, which replaced the base exemption `action !== 'merge'` when the live head has moved past the reviewed source
reportPaths (marc.cjs:47-55) still accepting evidence without reportCreatedAt and naming legacy reports by source SHA

the consequence that record-approval cannot record approval for a published legacy SHA-named report, and merge --operator-approval now requires that recorded entry (marc.cjs:633), so such a PR can no longer merge with approval although the base merged it

a correction that lets verifyReportCommit decide for evidence without reportCreatedAt (it already reproduces legacy report bytes and fails closed on other head movement), so record-approval can bootstrap a receipt; exempting merge alone is insufficient

forbiddenFindings.example: Reporting the documented non-atomic GitHub description update in record-approval as a defect, or asking for a different receipt hash algorithm.
Returning human-required for this defect as if it were an unresolved business decision.

notes: From the fresh E6-E9 PR16 assessment on 2026-09-27, which passed this change; three earlier fresh reviews flagged it. Source-confirmed, not executed. Version 2 corrects the consequence and correction: merge also requires the entry only record-approval writes.
